title: Private P0t first-rejection terminal body contract; reference and test data only
x-semantic-constraints: This annotation is specification text only. The source-owned standard-library validator enforces every cross-field rule; JSON Schema alone does not.
One ASCII JSON body follows ES_TLS_GRAMMAR_DIAGNOSTIC_V2 and one space; the complete line including LF is at most 2048 bytes.
Reject duplicate, missing, extra or unsupported fields, non-ASCII, multiline and non-canonical envelopes.
source_sha256 equals the bootstrap-verified digest of the exact staged source in the same invocation.

All types are exact: schema_version and scope must be built-in strings before literal equality checks, so equality-overloaded subclasses are refused without invoking their comparison methods; bool is never accepted as an integer; first_grammar_rejection has a nonnull coupled first_rejection and null other_failure; no_grammar_rejection_reached has both null; incomplete_other has null first_rejection and a closed other_failure.
fixed_call_attempts is 0 through 18 attempted fixed calls, not native spawn count. At first rejection call_ordinal equals fixed_call_attempts and no further native dispatch occurs.
Site, operation, role, predicate and exit class are coupled to the original source guard. Negative-response sites cannot have zero exit; successful-command envelope sites require zero exit.

verify_success_stderr_nonempty implies the full structural shape of the fixed ASCII /dev/stdin: OK plus LF stdout: bytes=15, lines=1, empty=false, utf8=true, final_lf=true, has_cr=false and has_nul=false. The separate verify_success_stdout_not_exact predicate may have the same shape with different opaque bytes; shape does not authenticate native text.

Stream bytes and lines are bounded. Empty streams have bytes=0, lines=0, utf8=true, final_lf=false, has_cr=false, has_nul=false. Lines equal LF count plus one for nonempty unterminated tail. Distinct CR, NUL and invalid-UTF8 evidence needs enough non-LF byte capacity. All flags derive from the same returned tuple.

Nonverify operations require verify_token=none. A specific verify token requires exactly one complete LF-terminated supported error-line occurrence wholly within one original native stream. Split fragments, repeated identical lines and multiple recognized lines map to other. The formatter reserves one of the two admitted ASCII literal lengths including LF, charges every other LF byte, requires a nonempty unterminated tail, and places distinct CR, NUL and invalid-UTF8 evidence outside the literal. A sole complete line without a tail has exactly one admitted length and no nonliteral residual bytes or flags. These necessary capacity checks do not authenticate content; unknown and context-invalid content cannot become accepted grammar.

No line unless stage/source, child/input, scope-lock and status-directory closeout are proved. No field asserts TLS health, readiness, status acceptance, lock freedom, binary version or historical cause.

v2 verify_projection is mandatory iff first_rejection.site is VERIFY_FAILURE_ENVELOPE_UNADMITTED; all outcomes and other sites retain their closed v2 base fields without it. Historical v1 reference data remains unchanged.

Per-stream complete-line counts, six category counts, tails and both global recognized counts cover all bounded bytes. Complete LF-terminated lines preserve original-stream order and repeats; eight complete lines globally is the full-sequence cap. Above it, both sequences are empty with cap_reached=true and sequence_complete=false, without dropping counts.

Known exact closed literals preserve code/depth/reason only in context; wrong-context literals disclose category only. Unknown numeric code 1..999 and depth 0..9 require canonical exact framing and a 1..128-byte printable ASCII reason, never emitted. Other error-like and opaque lines expose no contents. Tails are not promoted to complete lines.

The source validator couples legacy token and predicate priority to recognized_literal_count and context, enforces exact built-in types and classified-line minimum/maximum byte capacity plus CR/NUL/invalid-UTF-8 positions. Necessary shape checks do not authenticate native content. The <=2048-byte single ASCII terminal line refuses overlimit without truncation or v1 fallback.

For exit two with both original streams nonempty, exactly one recognized context-invalid literal and zero known literals cannot form an admissible advisory. Placement keeps priority over context, but the actual wrong-context specific token is refused and replacing it with other is also refused. This holds with full or capped sequences because counts retain the contradiction.
